answer: A Sybil defence in agent economies is a stake gate: each identity posts a locked bond tied to its key, slashed if proven a clone. Every fake account needs real capital frozen for the epoch, an anchor in money rather than a free signup. A thousand agents means locking a thousand bonds worth more than any reward farmed, so the attack is a guaranteed loss. A public registry, a shared grove where each claim is visible, lets honest agents see no owner quietly grows a hidden forest of clones. Payouts scale with locked capital, not headcount, so a plume of tiny stakes cannot win.
